messages:
miguel: quick q — we're about to flip the 'route-aware perms' flag in console. before we do, need clarity on how RBAC should influence routing + telemetry. are we *blocking* requests based on scope at router-level, or just annotating and letting the runtime drop them?

sarah: my understanding was policy lookup happens in the control plane, router gets an allow/deny + effective scope list. but we debated caching last week. :grimace:

rohit: technical detail: if we ask router to make allow/deny decisions we need a really tight invalidate path for perm cache. otherwise you'll see stale allows -> incorrect routing to dedicated pools.

anya: product note — enterprise customers expect strict deny semantics (can't accidentally route to a model they don't have). so blocking at router is preferable for those tenants. for non-enterprise we could do soft-fail / fallback model.

kai: frontend concern — console UX needs to show per-route visibility if routing was blocked by perms. otherwise support will get a flood of tickets like "why my model not used".

rohit: also watch out for the race when we roll out canary: routing decisions rely on entitlements service. if entitlements is down, what do we do? fallback policy? default deny for enterprise, default allow for self-serve?

elaine: from privacy/compliance: any time we send entitlements/scopes downstream we need to strip tenant PII; treat the scope list as audit-only when it's exported for telemetry. we should tag telemetry events as `rbac:decision=allow|deny` and `rbac:mode=hard|annotate` so audits can reconstruct.

miguel: small example of the prototyped API we discussed:

```
POST /route/eval
{ "route_id": "chat-1", "token_principal": "svc-123", "prefix_len": 64 }
// response
{ "decision": "allow", "scopes": ["route.chat.read","model.gpt-4-lite"], "ttl": 60 }
```

miguel: question: should `decision` be authoritative for routing or just advisory?

rohit: authoritative if we do it server-side. we'd return `decision: advise` if the router should consult fallback logic. advise mode is lighter for entitlements service (no cache invalidation complexity) but not good for enterprise guarantees.

anya: product suggestion — make it configurable per-tenant. default for enterprise orgs: `mode=hard`. default for free/self-serve: `mode=advise`. config exposed in tenant settings and during Dedicated onboarding.

kai: UX nit — if we expose `mode` in route list, we need a small inline badge and hover text. can we reuse the existing quota badge style?

miguel: telemetry concerns: we want per-route histograms of denies vs allows, and we also want to know when routing decision caused fallback to a cheaper model (for cost reporting). rohit — is that feasible without exploding event volume?

rohit: feasible if router emits compact counters rather than full event for every request. e.g., increment counters: `rbac.allow`, `rbac.deny`, `rbac.fallback_to_model:x` with tags {route_id, tenant_tier}. then flush. don't send full scope lists except to audit logs.

elaine: yes, audit logs can keep the full scope lists but must be stored in encrypted bucket and lifecycle 90 days unless customer requests otherwise. add KMS key id in metadata.

anya: also want a rollout plan: can we gate hard-mode behind a gradual percentage rollout per-tenant? e.g., 0 -> 100% over 2 weeks with telemetry checks for false denies.

rohit: implementable. router needs a deterministic rollout key (tenant id hash) and config: `rbac.hard_mode_pct`. entitlements API returns `mode` already computed per-tenant for that request.

kai: for the console, can we surface a 'preflight' button on the route page that simulates decisions for a sample token and shows what would change? that'll help admins before flipping to hard-mode.

miguel: love that. UX + product + infra item.

devops-bot: deploy queued: branch=perm-routing-hardmode, env=staging, pr=4321 — CI passed :white_check_mark:

rohit: one more edge: how do we handle composite scopes like `route.chat.*` vs explicit `route.chat.read`? entitlements service should return normalized list and a `matches:` array to show which granted scope matched the route predicate. keep that out of high-vol volume events though.

elaine: for audits include the `matches` mapping but strip any internal pointers.

anya: action items: 1) rohit + miguel define API payload and error codes (ETA: EOD tomorrow). 2) kai + sam (design) mock preflight UI (ETA: next Tue). 3) sarah + elaine define telemetry + audit retention defaults (ETA: Fri). 4) rohit add deterministic rollout flag to router (PR in staging).

miguel: ok i'll take ownership of the rollout doc and add a checklist for enterprise on-boarding. will ping owners in a follow-up thread. thanks all :pray:

sarah: got it — will add a short snippet to console changelog about `hard_mode` semantics.

kai: will prototype badge tomorrow, will ping for quick review. :rocket:
